solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A bit of body language

definitions.meaning: a part of the body, the muscular organ in the mouth
a ... is also a language, as in 'mother ...'

explanation.surface: Body language, such as a gesture, being described as just a small part of a wider vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the organ in the mouth, and a spoken language as in 'native tongue'.

clue.text: Basic tips for humanity

parts.note: 'basic' read as at the base: the tips at the very bottom of a human being are those at the ends of the toes

explanation.surface: Sounds like fundamental advice offered to all people.
explanation.definitionFit: Toe coverings are literally the tips of the feet, the lowest part or base of a person.

clue.text: Refinements of elegant neckwear

parts.note: elegant or fine can mean nice
ties are worn around the neck

explanation.surface: Describes the finer details of stylish ties and cravats.
explanation.definitionFit: Small refinements of manners or detail are the fine points of polite behaviour, synonyms.

clue.text: At university, eccentric master is against the current trend

parts.note: being 'up' is British usage for being in residence at a university

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd or off-centre, so the word master is rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky college don who refuses to follow fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the flow of a river means heading toward its source, the literal sense of the term.

clue.text: Coal rise affected heating units

indicators.note: affected means altered or worked upon, so the letters of coal rise are rearranged

explanation.surface: An increase in coal use changing how many heaters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are units of heat energy, used to measure the energy in food.

clue.text: Two bills I stuck on a tree

indicators.note: stuck on says the last letter is attached after what comes before
two signals that the abbreviation for bills appears twice in a row

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone pinning a couple of invoices to a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genus of thorny trees and shrubs, the wattle, common in Africa and Australia.

clue.text: Be too clever for Oxford University idiot

parts.note: a twit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A smart student outsmarting a foolish Oxford undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone by cunning is to be cleverer than them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: They join the family after the match

definitions.text: They join the family after the match

parts.words: They join the family after the match
parts.note: the match here is a marriage, which brings a spouse's relatives into one's family

explanation.surface: Sounds like fans joining a household after a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage become family once the wedding, the match, has taken place.

clue.text: Drink sounds dear to the French

indicators.note: sounds says the word is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: cheri is the French word for dear or darling

explanation.surface: A beverage that seems precious to French people.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fortified wine from southern Spain, a drink.

clue.text: Pardon and release

definitions.meaning: to forgive or overlook a fault
to let off from a duty

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both forgiving an offence and exempting someone from an obligation.

clue.text: French fortress, HQ until captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so one piece is taken within the other

parts.note: headquarters is a base
till means until

explanation.surface: A French stronghold remained the headquarters until it fell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789 at the start of the Revolution.

clue.text: Bloomers made by teachers having lost their head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: masters are schoolteachers

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by teachers who panicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like blunders, or knickers; it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden flowers are things that bloom, hence bloomers in crossword wit.

clue.text: Very serious internal trouble

parts.note: internal reads as within a nation, so the trouble is conflict among its own citizens

explanation.surface: Sounds like a grave medical complaint inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between factions of one country is the gravest kind of domestic strife.

clue.text: There's no straight solution to this clue

definitions.text: There's no straight solution to this clue

parts.words: There's no straight solution to this clue
parts.note: the answer is a word meaning not straight, bent or twisted

explanation.surface: A solver grumbling that the clue cannot be answered directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent or twisted is the opposite of straight, so the solution literally isn't straight.

clue.text: Maybe many decades are viewed in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the word are is read from the end

explanation.surface: Reflecting that a long stretch of years looks different with hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch can span many decades, so this is an example-based definition.

clue.text: One not going straight will have to make this up

definitions.text: One not going straight will have to make this up

parts.words: One not going straight will have to make this up
parts.note: a ship drifting sideways off course must make up the lost ground; also suggests a reformed criminal

explanation.surface: Sounds like an ex-convict who must make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways drift of a vessel off its course must be recovered, the idiom 'make up lost ground'.

clue.text: Wage rise? Just talk

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pay is a wage

explanation.surface: A cynic dismissing promises of a pay rise as mere chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter or idle noisy talk is a synonym, from the sound of a small dog.

clue.text: It's impossible to connect with this service

definitions.text: It's impossible to connect with this service

parts.words: It's impossible to connect with this service
parts.note: in tennis a serve the opponent cannot touch with the racket

explanation.surface: Sounds like a complaint about a phone or internet provider.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreturnable serve in tennis scores outright, since the receiver never makes contact.

clue.text: Island's chief accountant

parts.note: major means chief or principal
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Describes the head bookkeeper of some island firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Awkward ascent on railway line

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or out of shape, so the letters of ascent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy climb up a slope beside a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage or line of descent is one's family background, a synonym.

clue.text: It sounds highly unnatural

parts.note: highly refers to pitch: a male voice singing artificially above its natural range

explanation.surface: A remark that something seems very fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice forced above its natural register is high and artificial in sound.

clue.text: Dog loses tail — get it back!

indicators.note: losing the tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: An owner shouting at a dog that has hurt its tail to fetch something.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or fetch something is to bring it back, a synonym.

clue.text: Get out the cane, for example, or put into confinement

indicators.note: get out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A stern teacher reaching for the cane as a punishment, or locking someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out' rearranges CANE plus EG together.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut an animal or person in a cage is to confine them.

clue.text: Wells started writing in sudden bursts of activity

indicators.note: started says this piece begins the answer, ahead of the next

parts.note: spas are mineral springs or wells
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: The author H. G. Wells began his writing career in fits and starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden brief episodes of effort or energy, fits or bursts.

clue.text: Japanese copper married in the country

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a sen is a small Japanese coin, a copper being a low-value coin
wed means married

explanation.surface: A Japanese policeman got married abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer; here it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian nation in northern Europe, capital Stockholm.

clue.text: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps

definitions.text: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps

parts.words: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps
parts.note: a phrase meaning go away, which read literally tells a drummer to strike the drum

explanation.surface: A bandleader brushing off a percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang command to clear off reads literally as an instruction to hit something.

clue.text: Flycatcher

parts.note: not the bird but the spider's silken trap that catches flies

explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins its silk net precisely to trap flying insects.

clue.text: We assert he is a craftsman

parts.note: aver means to assert or declare

explanation.surface: A group declaring that a certain man is skilled at his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes cloth on a loom practises a traditional craft.

clue.text: Made up ground

definitions.meaning: wearing cosmetics, with face powder applied

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a face dusted with cosmetic dust, and a substance milled to fine dust.

clue.text: One who cuts corners — only one right turn

indicators.note: only one says one of the two letters for right must go, leaving the other
turn means the remaining letters are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A slapdash driver cutting corners, allowed just one right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNERS has two Rs; dropping one leaves CORNES, which 'turn' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who removes objectionable parts of films or books is one who cuts.

clue.text: Drug could have bearing on the case

indicators.note: on says the first piece sits before the next

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A medicine that might affect the outcome of a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing on the case' suggests relevance in court; 'case' is grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A calming medicine that induces sleep or relaxation is a type of drug.

clue.text: Not a figure of speech!

parts.note: figure taken literally: a sculpted human form, which cannot speak

explanation.surface: A pedant insisting something be taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure is silent, so it is literally a figure without speech.

clue.text: A tray's in use — should be clean

indicators.note: being in use means being worked, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of a tray's and in

explanation.surface: A tray that is being used ought to be hygienic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in use' does double work: 'in' is fodder and 'use' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygienic or free from dirt and germs, a synonym.

clue.text: My job envy lacks point, somehow

indicators.note: lacks says a letter must be taken away from the following words
somehow says the remaining letters fall into place in some new order

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone surprised that their jealousy of another's job seems pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like part of the fodder; it is the definition, an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of surprise, interjections with the same force.
